**Finding submitted: `missing` (IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data), confidence 0.82.**

What I found:
- **No ownership/assignment provision anywhere.** HDI designs, develops, hosts and operates the Site at its own cost (§§1.1–1.3), we supply all Content (§2.1), and HDI holds our user information and data (§8.1) — but the Agreement never says who owns the Site, the developed deliverables, or the customer/order data.
- **Nearby clauses don't cure it:** §5.2 gives us only artistic/editorial control; §8 gives only confidentiality; §10.2 disclaims co-ownership of the *relationship*, not of IP. The single express IP grant runs the other way — our "Deerskin" Marks licensed to HDI under §6.1.
- Nothing reaches even the fallback (a perpetual, royalty-free licence to use the deliverables), so the clause is treated as missing rather than a deviation.

Redline proposed (validated `ok:true`): new **Section 5.5 (Ownership)** inserted after §5.4, confirming we own the Content, Marks, the Site and other deliverables developed for us, and all user/order/transaction data, with HDI assigning any interest it holds; HDI keeps its pre-existing platform, tools and know-how and grants us a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense any of it embedded in the Site; joint ownership expressly excluded.
